body.statement: For the complete explicit three-copy relational forest instance with \(F(q)=\tfrac14+\tfrac12q-\tfrac13q^3\), there are source-reproducing endpoint groundings \(Z\) and a certificate \(Gamma\) with \(Check(S,G,Rsrc,Psrc,rho,a,B,Ictx,K,F,Z,Gamma)=1\), certifying \(Theta=[\tfrac14,\tfrac14+\tfrac{\sqrt2}{6}]\) and \(qplus=\tfrac{\sqrt2}{2}\). The checker rejects either a record selecting \(\tfrac14-\tfrac{\sqrt2}{6}\) or a record omitting the positive critical point.
body.justification: The cubic simultaneously tests an interior optimizer, an irrational endpoint, an extraneous conjugate, and exhaustive critical-point accounting.
body.gap: General algebraic procedures can verify the scalar identities, but no published relational certificate transaction includes the source-reproducing endpoint models.
body.consumer: This is the bounded implementation gate before applying the grammar to larger relational traffic groundings.
body.proof_tex:
We give the explicit forest instance.  In the source grounding, let
\(X_1,X_2,X_3\) be binary brake nodes with mutually independent fair
noises.  Let \(Y\) be a binary outcome whose supported conditional row
depends on the brake count \(k=X_1+X_2+X_3\) through
\[
 P(Y=1\mid X_1+X_2+X_3=k)=b_k,\qquad
 (b_0,b_1,b_2,b_3)
 =\left(\frac14,\frac5{12},\frac7{12},\frac5{12}\right).
\]
All displayed probabilities lie strictly between zero and one, so every
brake-count context has positive source probability and every source
joint cell on these four nodes is positive and rational.  The source law
is explicitly
\[
 P(X_1=x_1,X_2=x_2,X_3=x_3,Y=y)
 =2^{-3}b_{x_1+x_2+x_3}^{\,y}
       (1-b_{x_1+x_2+x_3})^{1-y}.
\]
It factorizes according to the acyclic graph and supplies the fair brake
row and all four outcome rows to \(K\).

In the target grounding attach two binary signal parents to each brake and
intervene to set all six signals to one.  The common brake type--context
row with two active signals is absent from every source occurrence; call
it \(rstar\) and write it as \((1-q,q)\).  The zero-signal brake row and
the four outcome rows are source supported, while the signal mechanisms
are removed by the intervention.  Hence \(rstar\) is the unique
target-relevant unsupported row.  The directed graph
\[
 \{\text{signals}\}\longrightarrow\{X_1,X_2,X_3\}
 \longrightarrow Y
\]
is acyclic, and its undirected ground graph is a tree with center \(Y\),
three brake neighbors, and two signal leaves adjacent to each brake.
The instance is therefore finite, Markovian, and type shared.

For \(B=\{Y=1\}\), the three target brake noises are independent and use
the same row.  Replaying the target factorization gives the Bernstein
polynomial
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 F(q)
 &=\sum_{k=0}^{3}b_k\binom3k q^k(1-q)^{3-k}\\
 &=\frac14+\frac12q-\frac13q^3.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Its derivative is
\[
 F'(q)=\frac12-q^2.
\]
The square-free cleared derivative \(1-2q^2\) has exactly one root in
\((0,1)\), namely
\[
 qplus=\frac{\sqrt2}{2},
 \qquad
 2qplus^2-1=0,
 \qquad
 \frac{70}{100}<qplus<\frac{71}{100}.
\]
The derivative is positive to the left of \(qplus\) and negative to its
right.  Direct evaluation gives
\[
 F(0)=\frac14,\qquad
 F(1)=\frac5{12},\qquad
 F(qplus)=\frac14+\frac{\sqrt2}{6}.
\]
Thus \(\texttt{thm:sharp-one-row}\) yields
\[
 \Theta
 =\left[\frac14,\frac14+\frac{\sqrt2}{6}\right],
 \qquad qminus=0.
\]
The upper value is the unique root in
\((48/100,49/100)\) of
\[
 144z^2-72z+1,
\]
whereas the conjugate root is
\(1/4-\sqrt2/6<1/4\).

For the lower endpoint, the brake-type breakpoint construction uses the
supported threshold \(1/2\) and the free threshold \(qminus=0\).  For the
upper endpoint, its distinct breakpoints are
\[
 0,\quad \frac12,\quad qplus,\quad1,
\]
with masses
\[
 \frac12,\qquad qplus-\frac12,\qquad1-qplus.
\]
The outcome-type breakpoints are all rational.  The inverse-threshold
mechanisms share these type tables across occurrences, and distinct ground
nodes receive independent copies.  The row calculations in
\(\texttt{thm:endpoint-models}\) show that both models reproduce the fair
source brake row, every supported outcome row, and hence every source
joint cell; their target values are the two displayed endpoints.  They
therefore serialize into a legal \(Z\).
\(\texttt{thm:certificate-completeness}\) supplies a \(\Gamma\) for this
fixed instance with
\[
 Check(S,G,Rsrc,Psrc,\rho,a,B,Ictx,K,F,Z,\Gamma)=1.
\]

Finally consider the two required rejection tests.  No feasible candidate
\(c\in\{0,1,qplus\}\) has
\(F(c)=1/4-\sqrt2/6\); indeed this conjugate lies below the already linked
boundary value \(F(0)=1/4\).  A record selecting it therefore fails either
the candidate-to-value link or the least/greatest linked-label check, so
soundness forces rejection.  If the positive critical point is omitted,
the certified Sturm count of \(1-2q^2\) on \((0,1)\) is one but the
purported exhaustive list contributes zero.  The candidate-exhaustiveness
check therefore rejects that record as well.
